perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s accessible perspective:

- He knows Gary Guo as a close, long-time friend from middle school; Gary is a doctor. They have relied on each other for emotional/professional support.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned about Gary’s health.
- Ethan invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation. Gary initially declined, saying he appreciated Ethan’s concern but had too much to do at the hospital. Ethan later was with Gary at the retreat.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected Gary’s overworking involved more than just professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, reminding him they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary said it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- After the confrontation, Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. Ethan felt relief and empathy and offered to help Gary find better balance.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed, saying he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself too.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed Gary’s progress and remaining challenges, saw Gary making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and continued offering support and encouragement.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, that he was less overwhelmed thanks to Ethan’s help, and that he had time for a movie last weekend.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing a healthier work-life balance and capable on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always just a call away. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.

Ethan does not have access to hidden events or private/narrator-only details not revealed to him through observation or conversation.
